To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SPARC expression in CMI is associated to imatib treatment and to the inhibition of leukemia cell growth and proliferation.

(1) low endogenous SPAR C expression is a constant characteristic of BCR/ ABL positive cells; (2) IM treatment induces SPAR C production by normal cells; (3) exogenous SPAR C inhibits CML cell proliferation; (4) exogenous SPARC synergizes with IM activity in vitro against CML.

SPARC is a protein with growth inhibitory and anti-angiogenic activity in several types of cells, and that in this work we have shown that in patients affected by CML the production of SPARC by the leukemic cells is low at the time of diagnosis and that it increases after the treatment with IM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of IM activity in CML and it could open new perspectives for the use of SPARC in CML treatment.
the identification of a potential new therapeutic target for CML treatment.
the possible role of SPARC in the treatment of CML and the potential use of SPARC in CML therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of SPARC in hematological malignancies is still controversial and that further studies are needed.
SPARC is a potential biomarker of IM treatment and that exogenous SPARC could be used in the treatment of CML.
SPARC may be considered a potential therapeutic target in CML.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SPARC expression in CMI is associated to imatib treatment and to inhibiting the leukemia cell proliferation.
